items.md: Global trends in mergers and acquisitions in the past ten years have been impacted by macroeconomic dynamics and the correlation between merger notifications and variables such as GDP growth, inflation and interest rates is strong. Periods of strong GDP growth tend to spur deals, while periods of recession or slower growth dampen them (see Figure 2.3). The most impactful shock in the last decade was the COVID-19 pandemic, where OECD jurisdictions observed a decrease of -4.75% in their GDP (and OECD estimates for the decrease in the World’s GDP were around 3% (OECD, 2020\[14]; 2021\[15]) that correlated with a drop in M&A activity in 2020 compared to 2019. In Latvia, the United States, Malta, the Slovak Republic and Greece, the increase was higher than 100% with respect to notifications in 2020.

In Latvia, the United States, Malta, the Slovak Republic and Greece, the increase was higher than 100% with respect to notifications in 2020.

After the two years with significant changes, 2022 presented a mixed picture.
